newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALIAN LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: The following matches are being played in Italy's Serie A this weekend (league positions in parentheses, all kickoff times GMT)

Bouyant Napoli, fresh from a midweek Italian cup semi-final qualification at the expense of Lazio, look to strikers Nicola Caccia and Fabio Pecchia and may have too much firepower for an Atalanta side led by winger Gigi Lentini but missing suspended Uruguyan defender Jose Herrera.

Multinational Inter should be able to make light of the absence of suspensed English midfielder Paul Ince against relegation battling Cagliari who look to the Uruguayans Fabian O'Neill and Dario Silva in attack.

Jet lagged Juventus, winners of the Intercontinental Cup Final against Argentine side River Plate in Tokyo on Tuesday, could have done without this home test against one of the most in-form sides of the moment. Croat Alen Boksic and Alessandro Del Piero lead the Juventus attack while Bologna, midweek Italian Cup semifinal qualifiers against Cremonese, rely as usual on Russian Igor Kolyvanov and Swede Kennet Andersson in attack.

One of the most intriguing ties of the day could see in form leaders Vicenza come unstuck against the unpredictable but attack-oriented Perugia. Croat striker Milan Rapaijc and the experienced ex-Inter and ex-Parma player Fausto Pizzi lead the Perugia attack against a full strength Vicenza led by Uruguyan Marcelo Otero and Roberto Murgita. Vicenza confirmed their current league form with a midweek Italian Cup quarter-final qualification at the expense of AC Milan.

Following yet another setback via a midweek Italian Cup elimination by Vicenza, Milan look to the league return of Montenegrin Dejan "The Genius" Savicevic to get them back on the winning path against all-Italian Piacenza led by striker Pasquale Luiso, on the seven goal mark. Milan may rest Roberto Baggio, recalling Marco Simone in his place alongside Liberian striker George Weah.

If current form is a guide, this will be the worst game of the day. Bottom club Reggiana sacked Romanian coach Mircea Lucescu in midweek, replacing him with Francesco Oddo. On Wednesday Lazio culminated a disasterous opening three months with elimination from the Italian Cup by Napoli. Giuseppe Signori and Pierluigi Casiraghi lead the Lazio attack while Reggiana look to the experience of Sandro Tovalieri up front.

Argentine Abel Balbo, Marco Delvecchio and Francesco Totti form a bold three man Roma attack in a game the home side need to win to keep their championship challenge on course. Full strength Fiorentina rely on Portuguese playmaker Rui Costa, Brazilian Oliveira and their Argentine captain Gabriel Batistuta, despite the latter's current poor form.

Parma may field a new attacking trio of Argentine Hernan Crespo flanked by Alessandro Melli with Enrico Chiesa playing just behind them. Udinese rely on German Oliver Bierhoff in attack, while both sides have one player suspended -- Parma midfielder Dino Baggio and Udinese defender Giovanni Bia.

Despite his apparant desire to head west to Spanish side Real Madrid, Sampdoria's French midfielder Christian Karembeu looks set to stay in Italy and should play on Sunday. Verona have picked up only one win in 10 games this season and are unlikely to improve on that record here.
